scope: Read-only retrospective six-hour capture/worker review, not the deferred 24-hour acceptance
observations: 20 queue maximum log records and 11 queue recovery records in the sampled log window; these are records, not counts of independent incidents.
Latest recorded queue recovery at 10:54:47/48 for both capture workers.
One rpicam timeout at 10:52:02 during the deployment backup window; temporal association is not proof of causation.
At 07:04:16 to 07:04:40, 23.885 seconds elapsed between Image processed and Compressed image file size logs.
At 07:04:57 to 07:05:36, 38.873 seconds elapsed between Adding image to DB and FRAME_METADATA logs.
These timings show processing_seconds alone omits material save/post-processing stalls.
Root filesystem 95% used, 5.6 GiB available; /tmp 5% used. No kernel warnings returned since 05:00.
At 11:09, the latest five saved images for each camera were exactly 15 seconds apart; camera1 latest 11:09:20, camera2 11:09:21.
conclusion: Transient delays persist after image publication fixes. A bounded syscall trace directly measured16.483467s in image-worker fdatasync on the database descriptor, consistent with WAL checkpoint cost. This identifies a blocking persistence stage; it does not establish the physical storage cause or prove all cadence incidents share it.
next_action: Verify WAL checkpoint ownership and move expensive checkpoint work out of the frame processing path with bounded background execution and recovery tests. Preserve synchronous=NORMAL and watchdog semantics; do not claim a fix before before/after measurement.
changes: No runtime/configuration changes, restarts or media deletions.
